items.title: ATMs Did Not Kill The Bank Teller
items.summary: In episode 1017 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, @JonKrohnLearns talks with Pete Johnson, Field CTO at MongoDB, about Jevons' paradox and its implications for AI's impact on the job market. Pete uses the compelling examples of bank tellers and toll booth workers to illustrate how making a resource (like human labor) more efficient with AI often leads to new uses and an overall increase in demand for that resource, transforming roles rather than simply eliminating them.

items.title: Why Neural Networks Feel Like Magic
items.summary:
Neural networks can seem mysterious at first — layers, weights, activations, training, backpropagation… it can feel like magic.

In this short, Luis Serrano, author of Grokking Machine Learning, Second Edition, explains the simplest way to start understanding neural networks: as systems that learn patterns step by step from examples.

Once you see the basic idea, the “magic” starts to feel much more understandable.

Book: https://hubs.la/Q04rsqf30

items.title: Don’t Train the LLM, Evolve the Harness: Inside "AutoDesign"
items.summary:
What if an AI could learn "human design language" without changing a single model (LLM) weight tensor? 

AutoDesign turns human preferences into executable evaluations, then uses them to evolve the harness surrounding a frozen LLM: rewriting how it transforms complex research into visual presentations. 

But is this machine creativity, or human taste compiled into code? Let’s open the black-box and find out.

items.title: The Hank Green Situation
items.summary:
Hank Green got “caught” using AI… and I genuinely don’t think he did anything wrong.

The whole controversy started because Hank said “I appreciate the pushback” in a video — a phrase people thought sounded suspiciously like ChatGPT.

That led to Hank explaining that while he doesn’t use AI to write his scripts, he DOES use it to help find research papers that he then reads himself.

And somehow, that turned into a much bigger debate about whether creators should be using AI at all.

I actually understand why people care. If you watch someone specifically for THEIR opinions, perspective, and commentary, you probably don’t want those things outsourced to an LLM.

But using AI as a better research tool or dumping your own messy thoughts into it and asking it to help organize them feels like a completely valid use-case to me.

I also think people need to give creators a little more grace here.

Creators are often working under a ton of pressure to constantly research, write, film, edit, publish, and somehow keep doing it over and over again while also having families, businesses, careers, and lives outside of what you see on camera.

Of course they're going to look for ways to make that process more optimized and sustainable.

Curious what your take on this is... 

#AI #Ainews

items.title: 3 New Ways To Use ChatGPT Codex
items.summary:
Most people are barely scratching the surface of what the new Codex app can do.

It can now browse social media without an API, turn something you build into a live, shareable website, and let you control work running on your computer directly from your phone.

To try it for yourself, you can use Codex with both the free and paid plans, although free accounts have lower usage limits and some features have separate requirements. 

Download the ChatGPT desktop app with the link in the pinned comment and try one of these today.

And SAVE this video to reference later.
